title: Slide whistle and kazoo players and tub bands
summary: Punch recalls a slide whistler, kazoo players played like trumpets and washboard tub bands.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, let me ask you something before you get up there. You're saying something about Joe Strutter back there.
No, I used to play them slide whistle.

Oh, yeah, yeah. He really could play that. I was going to play any tune in the band play. It used to take so long. Yeah. Tried the foot of one foot. Just playing the devil out of that whistle. And I used to wonder how he used to get up when I could play it down low. But to get up, you know. He used to go up like you go up on a horn. Teep. Do-do-dee-do-do-do-do. All like that. I couldn't do it.
I think you'd blow hard to do that or something.
I'd have to blow real hard to do that.
Yeah. But it looked like he used to bite on it or something.
What about kazoo? You were saying something about kazoo too.
No, he was asking me about, say some fella in the band, the chime on, bring him in on a kazoo.
Yeah, well he used to play them just like he played trumpet, you know.
George Brunny's a blue one. Yeah. They had many kazoo players around here?

Yeah, man. They had them little tub bands and. Kazoo, you used to play two of them. One, like you played, like you played a planet and a trumpet. One guy on a kazoo, was like, do Do do do do. Do do do. Yeah. He's a good guy. Washboard and all that stuff. Sounds good too, Paul. I'm telling you, these sound good. Did you?
We'll turn it off a second while you look for that, okay?
Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. 된 된 된 된 된
